chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who had a father who was a slave, and for his father was a wife, a contracted slave (mukattab) who had paid part of what was upon her. So the son of the slave said to her, 'Is it for you if I assist you in your contract until you pay what is upon you, with the stipulation that you do not have the choice regarding my father when you own yourself?' She said, 'Yes'. So he gave her in her contract, upon the stipulation that there is no choice for her upon him after she owns herself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The choice does not belong to her; the Muslims are upon their stipulations.'

key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: The right of choice or option, specifically here the wife's right to choose her master or leave.
key_terms.الْمُسْلُونَ عِنْدَ شُرُوطِهِمْ: The Muslims are upon their stipulations; a legal maxim validating contractual conditions.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٌ: Contracted manumission, where a slave agrees to pay a specific sum for their freedom.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on stipulating conditions in a slave's manumission contract (mukatabah) regarding the master's choice?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validated the son's stipulation that the freed slave woman would not retain the right of *ikhtiyar* (choice) to remain with or leave her former master, grounding the ruling in the general contractual principle 'Muslims are upon their stipulations.' This highlights the flexibility of *mukatabah* conditions in Shia jurisprudence, where specific agreements can modify standard manumission rights, reflecting the pragmatic application of Quranic and Prophetic precedents in family and property law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had a father of an owned slave, and for his father was a wife, a contracted slave girl, who had paid off part of what was upon her. So the son of the slave said to her, ‘Is it for you if I assist you in your contract until you have paid of what is upon you, with a stipulation that there does not happen to be the choice upon my father, when you own yourself’. She said, ‘Yes’. So he gave her in her contract, upon the stipulation that if there does not happen to be the choice for her upon him after she owns (herself). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There does not happen to be the choice of the submitters in their stipulations’.
